user_prompt:
Build an explorable three-dimensional world of a real place: 9 Ainslie Pl, Edinburgh EH3 6AT, UK. This is a continuous inhabited environment, not a picture of one. Every surface should hold up when approached closely and when viewed from any direction.

STRUCTURE AND MASSING
- **Typology & Provenance:** Neoclassical Georgian residential circus block, designed by architect James Gillespie Graham (1822) as part of the Moray Estate development. - **Storeys & Massing:** Symmetrical curved palace-front terrace consisting of a sunken basement, rusticated principal ground floor, piano nobile first floor, second floor, and an attic/blocking course storey. Advanced terminal and central pavilions break the curved facade plane. - **Vertical & Planar Alignment:** Rectified vertical load-bearing lines plumbed to true gravity vertical. Planar ashlar walls flattened from 3D scan distortions; horizontal datums restored along continuous stringcourses, sill bands, and projecting classical entablatures. - **Fenestration & Detailing:** Regular grid of timber sash-and-case windows (predominantly 6-over-6 and 12-pane configurations) recessed within dressed stone reveals. Piano nobile windows feature moulded architraves with projecting cornices. Cast-iron spearhead balustrades enclose sunken area wells crossed by oversailing ashlar entrance platts. Pitched slate roofs with dressed ashlar chimneystacks and cylindrical clay chimney pots.

SURFACES AND MATERIALS
- **Masonry Treatment:** Polished Craigleith ashlar with fine-tooled ashlar finishes on upper floors; deep V-jointed channelled rustication across the principal floor level. - **Roofing & Envelope:** Scottish Ballachulish and Welsh Penrhyn dark blue-grey slate tiles laid in diminishing courses, lead valleys, zinc/lead flashing, cast-iron rainwater goods with rectangular hopper heads. - **Environmental Pathology:** Stratified historical carbon and sulfur encrustation (gypsum black crusts) in sheltered lintel recesses and cornice undersides; surface rain-wash leaching across exposed ashlar faces; minor iron oxide staining and basal biological damp patina along plinth courses.

VEGETATION
- **Botanical Identity:** Mature urban garden specimens within Ainslie Place Gardens featuring *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), and *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm). - **Date-Grounded Phenology (September 3):** Full late-summer canopy volume with early transitional phenology; mature deep-green broadleaf foliage exhibiting incipient margins of chlorotic yellowing on upper exposed crowns; hanging clusters of dry samaras/keys; dense, manicured understory turf with perennial border plantings.
